```{r}
# visualisation 1: compare how raw data changed after it got cleaned
if (!requireNamespace("naniar", quietly = TRUE)) { install.packages("naniar")}
if (!requireNamespace("viridis", quietly = TRUE)) { install.packages("viridis")}

library(naniar)
library(viridis)

# in raw dataset, user_id had 0 NAs
# platform users --> platform_users_clean showed 200 rows being deleted. 
# gg_miss_var(platform_users) visualised 10 columns with NAs with max 20 NAs.
# this means there is 2 NAs per individual column, and no multiple NAs per row.

missing_comparison <- tibble(
  column = names(platform_users),
  raw_na = colSums(is.na(platform_users)),
  cleaned_na = colSums(is.na(platform_users_clean))
) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -column, names_to = "stage", values_to = "na_count") %>%
  mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = c("raw_na", "cleaned_na")))

ggplot(missing_comparison, aes(x = reorder(column, na_count), y = na_count, fill = stage)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Missing values: raw vs cleaned", x = "Column", y = "Count of NAs")

# comparison of columns with NAs and without more aesthetic commands
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis) # for color palette

#| fig.height: 10
#| fig.width: 8

plot_missing_comparison <- ggplot(missing_comparison, aes(x = reorder(column, na_count), y = na_count, fill = stage)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = na_count),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    hjust = -0.3,
    color = "black",
    size = 2.5
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "B", begin = 0.2, end = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 20)) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of Missing Values: Raw vs. Cleaned Dataset",
    x = "Column",
    y = "Count of NAs",
    fill = "Stage"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 14, family = "sans"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10), face = "italic", family = "sans"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10), face = "italic", family = "sans"),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, family = "sans"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, family = "sans"),
    text = element_text(family = "sans"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(
  filename = "visuals/missing_comparison.png",
  plot = plot_missing_comparison,
  width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)



# more code used to experiment, left in for future reference but not saved to folder
gg_miss_var(platform_users) 
# barplot per column
gg_miss_upset(platform_users) 
# overlap between NA columns



# Filter to only users with at least one NA
users_with_na <- platform_users %>%
  filter(if_any(everything(), is.na)) %>%
  select(user_id, everything()) 
# Keep user_id for plotting


summary_df <- tibble(
  stage = c("Raw", "Cleaned"),
  rows = c(nrow(platform_users), nrow(platform_users_clean)),
  rows_with_na = c(nrow(users_with_na), 0)
)

ggplot(summary_df, aes(x = stage, y = rows, fill = stage)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = rows), vjust = -0.5) +
  labs(title = "Data before and after cleaning", y = "Number of rows", x = "")


numeric_cols <- users_with_na %>% 
  select(where(is.numeric)) %>% 
  colnames()

```

```{r}
# back to platform_users_clean
# ggplot comparison: how does satiation_decay differ between pref_BeautyFashion and pref_Gaming per user. 
# 
# 1. mutate two new groups with users that prefer beauty/fashion over gaming and vice versa.
# 2. 

user_groups <- platform_users_clean %>%
  mutate(
    preference_group = case_when(
      pref_BeautyFashion > pref_Gaming ~ "Beauty/Fashion",
      pref_Gaming > pref_BeautyFashion ~ "Gaming",
      TRUE ~ "Neutral"
    )
  )

# Summary statistics
user_groups %>%
  group_by(preference_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_users = n(),
    mean_satiation = mean(satiation_decay, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_satiation = sd(satiation_decay, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_satiation = median(satiation_decay, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

satiation_pref <- ggplot(user_groups, aes(x = preference_group, y = satiation_decay, fill = preference_group)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, width = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Beauty/Fashion" = "#FF69B4", "Gaming" = "#4169E1")) +
  labs(
    title = "Satiation Decay by User Preference: Beauty/Fashion vs Gaming",
    x = "User Preference Group",
    y = "Satiation Decay",
    fill = "Preference"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(
  filename = "visuals/satiation_pref.png",
  plot = satiation_pref,
  width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)



# there is no noticeable difference in satiation decay between the two groups. so prefering one topic over the other does not have impact on satiation.
```


```{r}
# create random sample of platform_users_clean to not overcrowd pointplot
# 
set.seed(77) 
random_sample <- platform_users_clean[sample.int(nrow(platform_users_clean),800),]


library(tidyverse)

# seperate datatable for desired columns.
# goal: is there a correlation between beauty/fashion preference and the amount of videos watched?

cor_beauty_video <- ggplot(random_sample, aes(x = pref_BeautyFashion, y = base_videos_watched_mean)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 2, color = "#FF69B4") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#FF1493", fill = "#FFB6C1", alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation: Beauty/Fashion Preference vs Videos Watched",
    x = "Beauty/Fashion Preference Score",
    y = "Mean Videos Watched",
    caption = paste("Correlation:", round(cor(random_sample$pref_BeautyFashion, 
                                               random_sample$base_videos_watched_mean, 
                                               use = "complete.obs"), 3))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11)
  )

ggsave(
  filename = "visuals/cor_beauty_video.png",
  plot = cor_beauty_video,
  width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)

# no there is not, no clear trend visible. 




# goal: compare the top 100 pref.Gaming vs the top 100 pref.FashionBeauty based on interaction.
# from platform_users_clean, create two new datasets for "interaction and prefFashionBeauty" and "interaction and prefGaming"

# Top 100 Beauty/Fashion users
top_beauty <- platform_users_clean %>%
  arrange(desc(pref_BeautyFashion)) %>%
  slice(1:100) %>%
  mutate(group = "Top Beauty/Fashion")

# Top 100 Gaming users
top_gaming <- platform_users_clean %>%
  arrange(desc(pref_Gaming)) %>%
  slice(1:100) %>%
  mutate(group = "Top Gaming")

# Combine both groups
top_users <- bind_rows(top_beauty, top_gaming)

# Create point plot
beautyvsgaming <- ggplot(top_users, aes(x = need_interaction, y = group, color = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Top Beauty/Fashion" = "#FF69B4", "Top Gaming" = "#4169E1")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Need for Interaction: Top 100 Beauty/Fashion vs Top 100 Gaming Users",
    x = "Need for Interaction Score",
    y = "User Group",
    color = "Group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(
  filename = "visuals/beautyvsgaming.png",
  plot = beautyvsgaming,
  width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)

# also visualise grade of preference to see if there is a connection
```
